ACTION: ADD
TITLE: LoRA tuning of a 7B video-language model on gaze-marked questions
PROPOSAL: Build 12000 training questions about the wearer's fixation target and next action from the Ego4D gaze subset and EGTEA Gaze+, with the fixation drawn as a red circle on 8 sampled frames. Fine-tune LLaVA-OneVision-7B with LoRA for 2 epochs, using 5 seeds, and report accuracy on a held-out set of 1500 questions split by participant. The aim is to test whether a model that rarely saw gaze in pretraining can learn the marker.
CONTROLS: Same model tuned on the same questions with unmarked frames; zero-shot model given the marker; marker placed at a random location in the training questions
COST: 160
PREDICTION: The tuned model beats the zero-shot one by 8 to 15 accuracy points on fixation questions, with a smaller gain on next-action questions. The gain should vanish with the random marker, and it could fail if the marker coincides with a salient object.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Two-stage gaze alignment for a 7B video-language model on four egocentric corpora
PROPOSAL: Stage one trains the projector and LoRA weights of LLaVA-OneVision-7B on 40000 clip captions that name the object under the wearer's fixation, drawn from Ego4D, EGTEA Gaze+, Aria Everyday Activities and EPIC-Fields. Stage two tunes on 20000 intention questions about the wearer's goal, with 5 seeds. Results are reported on a held-out set of 1500 questions split by participant, with a table per corpus and per question type.
CONTROLS: Stage two alone from the base weights; stage one with shuffled captions from other clips; zero-shot model with a red circle on the frames; spread between seeds.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: The two-stage model beats stage two alone by 3 to 6 accuracy points on fixation questions, and shuffled captions remove the gain. The benefit could fail to carry over to corpora where recorded gaze is noisy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Zero-shot intent understanding without gaze in four open video-language models
PROPOSAL: Collect 1200 multiple-choice questions on the wearer's current goal, next action and object of interest from 300 clips of the Ego4D goal-step and EGTEA Gaze+ videos, with gaze removed. Evaluate Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL3-8B, LLaVA-OneVision-7B and VideoLLaMA3-7B on 16 uniformly sampled frames and report accuracy by question type, with 95 percent bootstrap intervals over clips. Annotators verify the correct option for 10 percent of items.
CONTROLS: Text-only prompting with the question and options, to measure language priors; random and majority-option guessing; a human reference on a 100-question subset.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Accuracy sits 15 to 25 points above chance but well below the human reference, with the weakest results on questions about fixation. It could fail if language priors alone already solve most options.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Frame-offset repeatability of intent answers from a 32B and an 8B video-language model
PROPOSAL: Score Qwen2.5-VL-32B and InternVL3-8B on 500 multiple-choice questions about the wearer's goal and next action, drawn from 150 Ego4D goal-step clips with gaze removed. Run the models 10 times with different 16-frame sampling offsets and with 3 wording variants of the prompt. Report mean accuracy by question type with 95 percent bootstrap intervals over offsets, and log the distribution of answer letters chosen.
CONTROLS: Text-only prompting with the question and options; random guessing; majority-option guessing; a human reference on 50 questions.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Accuracy varies by under 2 points over offsets, and both models land well above chance but well below the human reference. It could fail if the 32B model turns out no better than the 8B one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing four gaze presentation formats after tuning a 7B model
PROPOSAL: Build 3000 gaze-dependent questions from Ego4D gaze and EGTEA Gaze+ clips. Present the fixation four ways: a red circle on the frames, a crop around the fixation appended to the global frames, a blurred heat map blended into the frames, and text coordinates in the prompt. Tune Qwen2.5-VL-7B with LoRA on 2000 questions per format and test on 1000 questions held out by participant, with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Tuning on the same questions with no gaze information; a fixation marker at a random location; zero-shot model under all four formats
COST: 320
PREDICTION: Crop-plus-global and the circle beat text coordinates by 5 to 10 points, with the heat map in between. It could fail if the tuning set is too small to align any format.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Overlay versus coordinate text for a tuned 13B model with a longer schedule
PROPOSAL: Build 3000 gaze-dependent questions from Ego4D gaze clips. Compare a red circle overlay with text coordinates of the fixation in the prompt. Tune LLaVA-NeXT-Video-13B with LoRA for 6 epochs on 2000 questions and test on 1000 held-out questions, reporting accuracy by question type over 8 seeds. Training curves are logged and the best checkpoint is chosen on a 300-question validation split.
CONTROLS: Tuning with the same schedule and no gaze information, using identical frames; a random marker; coordinates shuffled across clips; zero-shot model.
COST: 320
PREDICTION: The overlay beats coordinates by about 6 points, and the gap persists on scene types not seen in tuning. It could fail if checkpoint selection on the small validation split overfits the 300 questions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sensitivity of a tuned gaze-aware model to gaze error at test time
PROPOSAL: Take the LoRA-tuned 7B model from the marker experiment and evaluate it on 1500 held-out questions with the fixation displaced by 0, 25, 50, 100 and 200 pixels, and with a fixation taken from a different clip. Report accuracy against displacement, with 95 percent bootstrap intervals over clips.
CONTROLS: The same model on frames with no marker; the same questions with a marker at the frame centre; a pretrained gaze estimation network run on the frames as a realistic noise source.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: Accuracy falls smoothly and reaches the no-marker level near 100 pixels. It could fail if the model already mostly ignores the marker.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Tuning gaze-aware models under matched noise levels
PROPOSAL: Tune 5 LoRA models of LLaVA-OneVision-7B whose training questions carry fixation noise of 0, 25, 50, 100 and 200 pixels, with 2 seeds apiece. Evaluate the models on 1500 held-out questions with clean gaze and with noise equal to their training noise, shown separately for clean and noisy test gaze. Report accuracy with 95 percent bootstrap intervals over clips.
CONTROLS: Tuning with no marker and the same seeds; a marker at the frame centre; a marker taken from a different clip.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: Models trained on noisier gaze lose little on clean test gaze. It could fail if noisy training makes the model discard the marker.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Generating and verifying a gaze-grounded question set with a 72B open model
PROPOSAL: Sample 4000 clips from Ego4D gaze and Aria Everyday Activities and mark the fixation on 8 frames per clip. Prompt Qwen2.5-VL-72B to write candidate questions about the wearer's focus, goal and next action, then run 3 verification passes in which the model answers with and without the marker and flags questions whose answer does not depend on gaze. Keep 5000 questions and have annotators check 400 of them.
CONTROLS: Question generation from unmarked frames; a 7B generator in place of the 72B one on 500 clips; agreement between annotators and the verification passes.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: About 40 percent of candidates are removed by verification and annotator agreement exceeds 85 percent. It could fail if the generator invents invisible objects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Large candidate pool for a gaze-grounded question set from a 32B open model
PROPOSAL: Sample 12000 clips from Ego4D gaze, EGTEA Gaze+ and EPIC-Kitchens with fixation overlays on 8 frames, and prompt Qwen2.5-VL-32B for candidate questions about focus, goal and next action. Apply 5 filtering rounds in which the model answers with and without the marker, and keep the 5000 questions that survive best, with a table per source. Annotators check 400 of them.
CONTROLS: Questions generated from unmarked frames; a 7B generator on 500 clips; annotator agreement with the filtering rounds on the checked questions.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Filtering removes roughly half of the candidates and annotator agreement exceeds 85 percent. It could fail if later rounds mostly remove questions that are hard rather than gaze-independent.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Screening out questions that can be answered without gaze
PROPOSAL: Run 3 video-language models (Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL3-8B, LLaVA-OneVision-7B) on the 5000 candidate questions twice, once with the fixation marker and once without, using 16 frames. Mark a question gaze-dependent when the marked version gains accuracy for at least 2 models. Keep those and report the share retained by question type.
CONTROLS: Text-only answering to find language shortcuts; a marker at a random location to find questions solved by the presence of a marker alone; manual review of 150 flagged questions.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Between 30 and 50 percent of questions are retained and location-only shortcuts account for under 10 percent. It could fail if the models are too weak to separate the two conditions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stability of the gaze-dependence screen over prompts and models
PROPOSAL: Run 6 video-language models of 7B to 8B parameters from distinct families, including Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3-8B, on the 5000 candidate questions twice, with and without the fixation marker, under 3 prompt templates and 16 frames. Mark a question gaze-dependent when the marked version gains accuracy for at least 4 models. Report the share retained by question type and the rank correlation between templates, and list the questions whose verdict flips with the template.
CONTROLS: Text-only answering; a marker at a random location; manual review of 150 flagged questions.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Between 30 and 50 percent of questions are retained, with rank correlation above 0.8 between templates. It could fail if the verdicts flip with the template.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gaze-region tokens appended to global tokens in a 7B video-language model
PROPOSAL: Encode a high-resolution crop around the fixation with the model's vision tower into 64 tokens placed after the global frame tokens. Fully fine-tune the language model of LLaVA-OneVision-7B on 60000 gaze-conditioned questions for 2 epochs, with 3 seeds. Evaluate on the 1500 held-out questions and on 2 external egocentric benchmarks.
CONTROLS: The same tuning with global tokens only; a red circle overlay; the crop taken at a random location; LoRA against full tuning on 10000 questions.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Crop tokens beat the overlay by 3 to 6 points on fixation questions and keep external scores within 1 point of the base model. It could fail if the longer context hurts performance on long clips.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Full fine-tuning of a 13B video-language model with gaze overlays on a large question mixture
PROPOSAL: Fully fine-tune LLaVA-NeXT-Video-13B on 90000 gaze-conditioned questions with a red circle overlay on 8 frames, for 3 epochs and 4 seeds, with checkpoints validated on 600 questions, using a cosine learning-rate schedule and a warm-up of 3 percent. Evaluate on the 1500 held-out questions and on 2 external egocentric benchmarks.
CONTROLS: The same tuning with unmarked frames; a marker at a random location; LoRA on 10000 questions; zero-shot model.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Gains over unmarked tuning reach 8 to 12 points on fixation questions and external scores stay within 1 point of the base model. It could fail if full tuning overfits the corpora's recording style.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training-free gaze prompting with demonstrations in three open models
PROPOSAL: Test whether in-context demonstrations teach gaze reading without any weight update. Give 3 open video-language models of 7B to 8B parameters 0, 2 or 4 solved examples showing a red-circle marker on the frames and the answer to a fixation question, then ask the 1500 held-out questions on 16 frames. Report accuracy by question type and number of demonstrations, with 3 prompt orderings and 95 percent bootstrap intervals over clips.
CONTROLS: Demonstrations with markers in wrong places; demonstrations without markers; zero-shot with the marker; text-only answers.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Two demonstrations lift accuracy by 3 to 7 points and 4 add little more. It could fail if the demonstrations consume context that the clips need.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Zero-shot comparison of marker colours and sizes on a 7B model
PROPOSAL: Check whether the look of the marker changes how a model reads it. Overlay a circle in red, green or yellow with radius 20, 40 or 60 pixels on 16 frames of the 1500 held-out questions and query Qwen2.5-VL-7B and LLaVA-OneVision-7B. Report accuracy by question type for the resulting appearances, with prompt orderings and 95 percent bootstrap intervals over clips. Frames, questions and decoding settings stay identical across appearances so that only the marker changes.
CONTROLS: No marker; a marker at a random location; text coordinates; an arrow in place of the circle.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: Accuracy differs by under 3 points over appearances, with the larger radius slightly better. It could fail if one colour blends into common backgrounds.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer of a gaze-tuned model to two external egocentric benchmarks
PROPOSAL: Tune LLaVA-OneVision-7B with LoRA on 15000 gaze questions mixed with 15000 general egocentric questions to limit forgetting, with 3 seeds. Evaluate on EgoSchema, EgoTextVQA and the held-out gaze set, with and without the marker, using 16 frames, a fixed prompt template and the same decoding settings.
CONTROLS: Tuning on general questions only; tuning on gaze questions only; the base model.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: The mixed model keeps EgoSchema and EgoTextVQA scores within 1 point of the base model while gaining on gaze questions. It could fail if the gaze data shifts the answer style on external sets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Wide benchmark sweep for a gaze-tuned 7B model
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the tuned LLaVA-OneVision-7B and its base on 6 benchmarks (EgoSchema, EgoTextVQA, EgoPlan, MVBench, Video-MME and the held-out gaze set), under 5 frame budgets from 8 to 64 frames and 3 seeds, supplying gaze predicted by a pretrained estimator where the marker is used. Report scores with bootstrap intervals and the change from base.
CONTROLS: The base model; tuning on gaze questions only; a random marker.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Scores change by under 1.5 points on non-gaze benchmarks and rise on the gaze set over frame budgets. It could fail if predicted gaze adds noise on third-party videos.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does the fixation land on the object the question is about
PROPOSAL: For 2000 clips with recorded gaze, run Grounding DINO on the frame at the question time with the object phrase and compute the share of fixations inside the box or within 50 pixels, by question type. Fit a logistic regression that predicts correctness from this overlap using zero-shot results of Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3-8B.
CONTROLS: Fixation from another time in the same clip; fixation from a different clip; box centre shifted at random.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Overlap exceeds 60 percent for fixation questions and stays under 30 percent for scene questions. It could fail if the detector misses small objects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Segmentation-based overlap between fixation and question targets
PROPOSAL: For 2500 clips with recorded gaze, prompt SAM 2 with Grounding DINO boxes for the object phrase and compute the share of fixations inside the mask at 5 time offsets before the question, from 0 to 4 seconds. Fit a logistic regression that predicts correctness from overlap using zero-shot results of 4 models of 7B to 8B parameters, with 3 bootstrap resamples of the clips.
CONTROLS: Fixation from another time in the same clip; fixation from a different clip; mask centre shifted at random.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Overlap peaks at the shortest offset and falls below 40 percent at 4 seconds. It could fail if mask quality varies by object class.
